summary: The figure shows the probability of dying from the four major noncommunicable diseases (cardiovascular disease, cancer, chronic respiratory disease, and diabetes) between ages 30 and 69 years across WHO regions and globally from 2000 to 2048. Observed data from 2000 to 2019 show a general decline in mortality probability in all regions. Projections based on observed trends suggest a slower decline, while the required trajectory to meet the SDG3.4.1 target demands a steeper reduction by 2030. The African and Eastern Mediterranean regions have the highest probabilities, while the Region of the Americas and European Region show lower probabilities. Globally, the probability is declining but needs to accelerate to meet the SDG target.
